<?php
$s = trim(fgets(STDIN));
$len = strlen($s);
$n = intval(trim(fgets(STDIN)));

function check_val($a, $s, $len, $n) {
    for ($i = 1; $i <= $a - $n; $i++) {
        if ($s[$len - $i] !== $s[$len - $i - $a]) {
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}

$ans = 0;
$temp = 0;

if ($n > $len)
    $min = intdiv($len + $n, 2);
else
    $min = $n;

$max = intdiv($len + $n, 2);

for ($i = 0; $i < $len; $i++) {
    for ($j = 1; $j * 2 + $i <= $len; $j++) {
        $key = 1;
        for ($k = 1; $k <= $j; $k++) {
            if ($s[$i + $k - 1] !== $s[$i + $k + $j - 1]) {
                $key = 0;
            }
        }
        if ($key == 1) {
            if ($j > $temp) {
                $temp = $j;
            }
        }
    }
}

for ($i = $max; ($i >= $min) && ($ans == 0); $i--) {
    if (check_val($i, $s, $len, $n) == 1) {
        $ans = $i;
    }
}

if ($min > $ans)
    $ans = $min;
if ($temp > $ans)
    $ans = $temp;

echo (2 * $ans);
?>

source_data.prob_desc_description: Kolya got string s for his birthday, the string consists of small English letters. He immediately added k more characters to the right of the string.Then Borya came and said that the new string contained a tandem repeat of length l as a substring. How large could l be?See notes for definition of a tandem repeat.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print a single number — the maximum length of the tandem repeat that could have occurred in the new string.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains s (1 ≤ |s| ≤ 200). This string contains only small English letters. The second line contains number k (1 ≤ k ≤ 200) — the number of the added characters.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteA tandem repeat of length 2n is string s, where for any position i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) the following condition fulfills: si = si + n.In the first sample Kolya could obtain a string aabaab, in the second — aaabbbbbb, in the third — abracadabrabracadabra.
